title: (Kanienʼkéha) Animal Nation
description: (Kanienʼkéha, Kanien'kéha (Kahnawà꞉ke and Six Nations)) A cross-Canada journey reveals how beavers shape ecosystems, restore wetlands and connect Indigenous communities to the land. From Algonquin Park, Ont., to Nicola Valley, B.C., the industrious.

title: (Blackfoot) Secret History
description: (Blackfoot, Siksika) After saving her father's life in an Assiniboine attack, a young Blackfoot girl is honored with the prestigious warrior name Pi'tamaka (Running Eagle).

title: (Blackfoot) Poke'n the Bear
description: (Blackfoot, Siksika) Community politics isn't just band office gossip. This episode pulls back the curtain on tribal politics - the drama, the deals and the disappointments. There's no shortage of conflict. But is there real progress?

title: (Michif) Michif Country
description: (Michif, French) Michif Country welcomes Anishinaabe singer-songwriter Leonard Sumner for a white-tailed deer hunting adventure near St. Laurent. Alongside Elder Earl St. Goddard and some of his family, Leonard reconnects with nature and gains.

title: (Michif) Red River Gold
description: (Michif, French) Memphis and Goldie travel a piece of the trail in an authentic Red River cart, and an 1800s weigh station at a river crossing yields interesting finds.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Quest Out West Wild Food
description: (Nsyilxcen) Tracey returns to an ancestral gathering place to talk about its significance and then visits another culturally important site with Carrie Terbasket to discuss preservation efforts in the area. Tracey reconnects with her cousins.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Quest Out West Wild Food
description: (Nsyilxcen)Tracey visits the Lower Nicola Indian Band and speaks with Chief Stuart Jackson about the devastation caused by recent climatic events.Tracey then meets Lorna Shuter,operator of Shulus Gardens, and cooks a meal with the band school's chef.

title: (Nsyilxcen) Merchants of the Wild
description: (Nsyilxcen) Deadly currents and harsh weather wreak havoc on the group's latest paddle. An imperative Elder teaching focuses on animal hide. As the season changes and storms threaten the valley, the group must work harder than ever to survive.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Teepee Time
description: (Mi'kmaq) Spend time with Teepee as he picks a pumpkin and chooses a costume for the very first time.

title: (Wolastoqey) Lil Glooscap and the Legends of Turtle Island
description: (Wolastoqey) The kids learn that all families are unique and made up of different types of people. The differences only make a family stronger! What's important is that families work together to take care of each other.

title: (Inuktitut) Tuktu
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Tiri feels left out when he returns from a trip with his family to see that his friends have made a new friend, Natsiq. Tiri feels left out but is encouraged to give Natsiq a chance. Tiri works hard to get to know Natsiq.

title: (Inuktitut) Anaana's Tent
description: (Inuktitut, North and South Baffin) Last night, Rita Claire and Qimmiq were able to see the Northern Lights, so the days must be getting shorter. We learn a legend about the Northern Lights and read the book Tuktu's Journey.

title: (Cree) Tiga Talk
description: (Cree) Tiga and friends make fall decorations and learn about hibernation. Kokum and Tiga meet an artist who makes prints of salmon swimming upstream, and before bed, she shares her favorite fall memories with the children.

title: (Anishinaabemowin) Chums
description: (Anishinaabemowin, Central) In an uplifting quest, the Chums encounter a moose eager to participate in the Moose Horn Festival. They embark on a musical journey, teaching and learning animal calls together to ensure his dazzling festival debut.

title: (Halkomelem) Coyote's Crazy Smart Science Show
description: (Halkomelem) Isa introduces us to the world of skateboarding and our Science Questers learn how physics, force, energy and gravity are in motion while skateboarding - all while having fun doing ollies!

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Dreamcatchers
description: (Kanienʼkéha) When the Dreamcatchers catch a dream about a giant robot destroying the city, they must find the Dreamer, unlock his ancestral superpowers and stop the dream from coming true!

title: (Inuktitut) Warrior Up!
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Kya Steinbach-Parker, aged 17, is a determined education activist who successfully lobbied for an Indigenous history class in her high school. Her goal is to help her province achieve the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

title: (Inuktitut) Ajungi!
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Eunice Tungilik teaches Abby Javagiaq how to make traditional Inuit fur mittens for a little girl.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Princesses
description: (Kanienʼkéha) Sexuality in Indigenous communities is a very touchy and rarely discussed subject. How does one balance having a healthy sexual identity as well as being part of a marginalized group such as Indigenous women?

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Working It out Together
description: (Kanienʼkéha) Waneek introduces The Fab Four team to yoga in the park. The girls are also treated to a lesson on superfoods, picnic-style. We meet Alexa and learn her reason for taking the Working It Out Together challenge.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) One Dish, One Spoon
description: (Kanienʼkéha) Still grieving, Tawnya pushes through exhaustion to cater the Sapling & Flint Winter Market, feeding her community and remembering her mother's impact.

title: (Cree) Indians and Aliens
description: (Cree) Ernest travels to Lake Timiskaming First Nation, an Algonquin community in Ontario. There, he meets with James Simpson, a retired Algonquin police officer, and hears about his heart-pounding encounter with a lake monster in Lake Timiskaming.

title: (Cree) Pow Wow Chow
description: (Cree, Swampy) Short on spuds, Bob buys into a unique program at Rama, while Shawn's brother Howard practices his Ojibway on customers.

title: (Michif) Métis Foodies
description: (Michif, Heritage) Suzanne and Paulette visit the Houle family in Calgary, where they celebrate the legacy of legendary fiddler Teddy Boy Houle. Through music, food, and family stories, they honour Métis tradition and the bonds that keep it alive.

title: (Michif) Chaos and Courage
description: (Michif) Meet the EMTs at La Ronge Emergency Medical Services in northern Saskatchewan, who face the perils of remote rescue and do whatever it takes to transport their patients to safety - whether by ambulance, snowmobile, plane or on foot.

title: (Salish) Warrior Games
description: (Salish) Host Steve Sxwithul'txw joins a group of Inuit youth to learn Arctic games, quickly realizing that it's far harder than it looks to kick something six feet in the air from a kneeling start. To help save his bruised ego, he tries his hand.

title: (Nisga'a) Ocean Warriors: Mission Ready
description: (Nisga'a) A floatplane with four people aboard reports a hard ocean landing, flipping over in an area of turbulent riptides. The Quatsino Nation Coast Guard Auxiliary joins the Gordon Reid Canadian Coast Guard Ship to search for the downed plane.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Gespe'gewa'gi: The Last Land
description: (Mi'kmaq) Rock crab season is just around the corner, and it's the perfect time for the community powwow. Powwow organizer Lita Isaac and her powwow family prepare for the festivities as the weekend unfolds and deal with some surprise weather.

title: APTN National News Weekend
description: Bringing the week full circle with a recap of the top national news stories of the week.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Gespe'gewa'gi: The Last Land
description: (Mi'kmaq) In this episode, Captain Preston Paul embarks on a week-long shrimp fishing expedition on a vessel called the Migmawei Amstel. A sudden storm challenges his inexperienced crew, but friendly competition on the boat keeps their spirits high!

description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) Natti gets frustrated when she's forced to shovel the walkway before joining her friends in the snow. Meanwhile, Taqu spots a special carving made by Vivi's dad, with strict instructions from Vivi not to touch it.

title: (Inuktitut) Ukaliq and Kalla
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin)Summer has arrived in the Arctic!Kalla reminds Ukaliq of all the summer activities after warning him not to snowmobile on broken sea ice.while boating,the friends collect icebergs for water and discover it makes the best tea.

description: (Cree) Come sing and dance with Bizou as she takes you on a picturesque journey into the wonderful world of Polar Bears, the Arctic's lumbering giant.

title: (Cree) Coyote's Crazy Smart Science Show
description: (Cree) Virtual reality technology can help us experience stories and reconnect with the land. In this episode, the Science Questers speak with Indigenous VR experts about how youth can make their own VR and how VR is being used to teach language.

title: (Kanienʼkéha) Dreamcatchers
description: (Kanienʼkéha) All that glitters is not gold! The Dreamcatchers strive to halt an earth-shattering mining operation, joined by a flippant young dreamer more interested in fun. Together, they work to preserve the local ecosystem.

title: (Inuktitut) Uakallanga
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) In this episode, mother-daughter duo Jo Ellen Etuangat and Taukie Etuangat make a child's growth chart on a canvas with the design of a narwhal and its long ivory tusk. This design can be made at home with some craft.

title: (Inuktitut) Nunavummi Mamarijavut
description: (Inuktitut, South Baffin) In this episode of Nunavummi Mamarijavut, we watch a beluga whale being harvested and then host Zipporah Ungalaq learns how to make beluga whale jerky from Nate Jewett in Iqaluit.

title: (Innu-aimun) Chuck and the First Peoples' Kitchen
description: (Innu-aimun, Uashat and Pessamit) Chuck goes to Dettah, a Dene community in the Northwest Territories, for some net fishing with Bobby Drygeese. His camp sits on Great Slave Lake, known for its giant trout. They don't catch any trout, but pull in.

title: (Innu-aimun) De Pessamit à Sheshatshiu
description: (Innu-aimun, Uashat and Pessamit) Moïra rencontre le chef de Sheshatshiu qui lui dévoile ses préoccupations pour la santé des siens. Elle rencontre plusieurs Innus de sa génération post-nomade,qui campent à Gull Island pour parfaire leur cheminement.

title: (Cree) Red Earth Uncovered
description: (Cree, Plains) Shayla explores the Kamloops area and learns more about the legends after speaking with a coyote expert.

title: (Cree) Wild Rose Vets
description: (Cree, Plains) Volunteering with the Mission PAWSible mobile vet unit in a remote Indigenous community, Dr. Emma manages loose dogs getting rowdy at the clinic. A routine spay takes a shocking turn when she finds a bullet in a dog.

title: (Michif) Amplify
description: (Michif, French) Anishinaabe electro-pop artist Wolf Saga draws inspiration for his music from a painting his grandmother bought, which connects him to his culture. This episode features Richard Gracious, Janis Monture, Elder Mary Lou Smoke.

title: (Michif) Nation Untamed
description: (Michif, Heritage) Sam and Chuck head to Lac du Flambeau in Wisconsin, where they head out onto the dark, frozen lakes to learn how to fish giant muskellunge. This fish is particularly special to the Ojibwe, who have traditional ways of hunting it.

title: (Salish) Warrior Games
description: (Salish) Host Steve Sxwithul'txw joins a group of Inuit youth to learn Arctic games, quickly realizing that it's far harder than it looks to kick something six feet in the air from a kneeling start. To help save his bruised ego, he tries his hand.

title: (Halkomelem) Nations at War
description: (Halkomelem) The French and British Empires took up arms over Nova Scotia in the 18th century. Caught in the middle, the Mi'kmaq Nation waged a guerrilla resistance against genocidal British officers and lethal American rangers.

title: (Wolastoqey) Petroglyphs to Pixels
description: (Wolastoqey) Cori stands out as a highly regarded carver in a field historically dominated by men. She honed her skills under master carver and mask maker Reg Davidson, earning respect and recognition.

title: (Mi'kmaq) Spirit Talker
description: (Mi'kmaq) Shawn celebrates National Indigenous Peoples Day with Acadia First Nation in Nova Scotia. The spirit of a young woman who died of cancer shares her sense of humor with her mother and siblings, and a close sisterly bond is renewed.
